chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): In

a man who had to fast 'two consecutive months' as expiation for Dhihar, and he fasted Dhu al-Qi'dah and Dhu al-Hijjah entered upon him - what should he do? He said: 'He should fast all of Dhu al-Hijjah except the days of Tashriq, then make up for them on the first day of Muharram until he completes three days, so that he has fasted two consecutive months.'

Then he said: 'And it is not appropriate for him to approach his wife until he makes up the three days of Tashriq that he did not fast, and there is no harm if he fasted a month, then fasted some days from the following month, then an excuse presented itself to him to break it, then he makes up the remainder of the month afterwards.'

key_terms.أَيَّامَ اَلتَّشْرِيقِ: days of Tashriq (11th, 12th, 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.ظِهَارٍ: Dhihar (a form of pre-Islamic/early Islamic divorce by analogy)

ai.seo_question: How to make up missed consecutive fasting days for Dhihar expiation?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling in *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* to clarify the continuity (*ittisal*) requirement for the two-month expiation of *Dhihar*, specifically addressing the interruption caused by the prohibited days of Tashriq. The scholar emphasizes that the makeup days in Muharram must be fasted immediately after the remaining days of Dhu al-Hijjah to maintain the consecutive nature of the fast, and sexual intimacy remains prohibited until this specific sequence is fully completed.
